slug: 2026-03-31 Africa we have a data problem

facts.fact: The essay's Somalia registry row, an AI-assisted compilation by its own header, states that rural registry offices (district or local municipal offices) rely on paper forms for births and that most rural registration remains paper-based; it gives no date for this, so the document's published date is used.
The essay's Somalia registry row states, citing OpenCRVS's country story, that more than 28,000 births had been registered digitally through OpenCRVS by 2026; it mentions no deaths.
The essay's Somalia registry row states, citing OpenCRVS's country story, that births are registered digitally at the point of service into a central database (2026).

The essay's Somalia registry row states, citing OpenCRVS's country story, that OpenCRVS runs as digital pilots in 30 districts, many of them rural, with 160 hospitals linked (2026); it gives no total of districts or offices and says the pilots cover a minority of facilities.
The essay's Somalia registry row states, citing SONNA, that the system was launched in 19 districts including rural ones (Abudwaq, Hudur and Kismayo are named) in August 2025; it gives no total.

systems.tiers: 30 districts, many rural, with 160 hospitals linked; launched in 19 districts in August 2025

note: Passages only. The source is listed in study.json's exclude_sources as an AI-assisted compilation; its facts are recorded as what it states and each says so. It calls the OpenCRVS deployment 'digital pilots'. It also mentions a CRVS policy and law (2021 onward) and a 2024-29 plan without saying the plan names the system, so no governance fact is taken; and a UNFPA 2021 statement of no national CRVS office and an unimplemented digital repository policy, and 3.5% of under-fives registered (SHDS 2020), which are not office facts.
